harvestMonths.region: South Africa (general — Mpumalanga lowveld, Limpopo, KZN coast)

evidence.quote: Lychees mature between November and February with a peak in December and January.
evidence.doc: Menzel, C., 'Lychee Growing and Marketing in South Africa', The Archives of the Rare Fruit Council Australia, July 1995 (production regions cited: Eastern Transvaal Lowveld, Northern/North-Eastern Transvaal, North and South Coast of Natal)

harvestMonths.notes: Consistent with an independent industry summary found (not directly fetched/quoted so not used as primary evidence here) that the SA litchi season 'begins around mid-October in the early areas of Malelane and Komatipoort in Mpumalanga, peaks in December and ends around the end of February' in Nelspruit/Tzaneen/Louis Trichardt — i.e. slightly earlier-starting in the hottest lowveld pockets than the Nov-Feb figure used here.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: Not sourced to standard. General web claims of '5-8 years to full production' for litchi could not be traced to a verbatim quote in an ARC-ITSC, SALGA or peer-reviewed document that was actually fetched during this research pass; ISHS articles on the SA litchi industry and irrigation ('THE SOUTH AFRICAN LITCHI INDUSTRY - AN OVERVIEW', 'IRRIGATION OF LITCHIS IN SOUTH AFRICA') were only accessible as abstracts (full text is behind an Acta Horticulturae paywall).

yearsToFullBearing.notes: Same access limitation as yearsToFirstCrop above.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Found mature tree spacing (12 x 12 m = 64 trees/ha, with some growers planting 6 x 6 m and thinning to that at year 15) and industry-wide totals (~8000 tonnes from ~1500 ha) in the Menzel (1995) article, but did not use these to derive a kg/tree figure because the tonnage is an all-ages industry average, not a stated mature-tree/mature-orchard yield, and converting it would misrepresent an industry mean as a per-tree mature yield.

chillUnits.notes: Litchi flower-induction is known in the wider horticultural literature to require a period of cool, dry winter weather, but no ARC-ITSC/SALGA/peer-reviewed South African source giving a specific temperature threshold or chill-unit/chill-day count for litchi floral induction was fetched and verified during this pass, so left null rather than repeating an unverified figure.

pollination.notes: Set to null in editor review: the quote is a reformatted table of flower-visitor shares (honeybee 65%...). It does not state whether a single litchi tree sets fruit alone. Withdrawn value: partly-self-fertile.

gaps: Full text of ISHS/Acta Horticulturae articles ('THE SOUTH AFRICAN LITCHI INDUSTRY - AN OVERVIEW', 'IRRIGATION OF LITCHIS IN SOUTH AFRICA - AN OVERVIEW') is paywalled; only abstracts were accessible, so years-to-bearing, yield/tree and chilling data likely contained in these could not be extracted.
arc.agric.za/arc-itsc/Pages/Litchi.aspx (ARC-ITSC's own litchi page) returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable when fetched.
SALGA's own site (litchisa.co.za) was found in search results but not fetched directly for a production guideline; worth trying in a follow-up pass.

No SA-specific, verifiable number found for years to first crop, years to full bearing, yield per mature tree, or a litchi chill-unit/chill-day requirement despite multiple searches; all left null per instructions rather than guessed.
Editor review 2026-09-28: pollination withdrawn — the flower-visitor table does not support a self-fertility claim.
